Command.description:
Every command, tagged by `type`. Each variant's schema title names the
Python client's class for it (`StreamPutCommand`), and its `type` names
the client's method: `domain/verb` is `client.domain.verb(...)`, a type
without a slash a method of the client itself.

oneOf.description: `ping`: answered with `pong`, not a `result`.
oneOf.title: PingCommand

oneOf.description: `info`: version, build, schemes, outputs, codecs, limits and sandbox.
oneOf.title: InfoCommand

oneOf.description: `metrics/get`: process, worker and stream counters.
oneOf.title: MetricsGetCommand

oneOf.description: `schema`: the JSON Schema bundle of every message.
oneOf.title: SchemaCommand

oneOf.description: `stream/put`: the idempotent upsert of a stream's desired state.

orientation.description:
How the picture is turned for display. A change reaches the open
sessions too, from their next frame and without a new answer.
Changing only this never reconnects.

preload.description:
Keep the source connected without viewers: connected at put and
reconnected after failures while set, so the first viewer gets a
frame from the warm GOP cache. Changing only this never reconnects;
turning it off with no viewers starts the linger.

sources.description: The sources, in order; the first that provides a kind wins.

ConnectionInfo.description:
The upstream connection behind a source: the stream's own, since a
source URL belongs to one stream (`source_in_use`).

DemuxMetrics.description:
The supervisor's demux counters: what the receive thread did with each
datagram on the shared UDP socket.

addresses_learned.description: Addresses learned through verified STUN requests.

relay_discarded.description:
Datagrams from a TURN server discarded: not on a held channel, not
from a permitted peer, or neither STUN nor `ChannelData`.

relayed.description: Datagrams a TURN server relayed from a peer, unwrapped and routed.

responses.description: Responses to the supervisor's own STUN and TURN requests.

stun_rejected.description: STUN requests with an unknown ufrag or a wrong password.

unroutable.description: Datagrams from unknown addresses that were not a usable STUN request.

worker_full.description: Datagrams dropped because the worker's channel was full.

ErrorCode.description: Every stable error code. `code` is the contract; `message` may change.

api.description:
The API version (Semantic Versioning, [`crate::API_VERSION`]); a client checks it
with [`crate::ApiVersion::accepts`].

features.description: Capabilities inside outputs, for a client to gate features on.

oneOf.description: The only value.

IceServer.description:
One entry of `webrtc/offer`'s `ice_servers`, as the client forwards what it
gave the browser (the W3C `RTCIceServer` dictionary). `Debug` redacts the
credential.

schemes.description: The URL schemes a client may route here.

abi.description: The kernel's Landlock ABI; zero without Landlock.

LastError.description: The last error of a stream, or the connection it reads from.

session_grace_ms.description: How long an orphaned session outlives its connection.

sessions.description: Open viewer sessions on all connections.

workers.description: The running workers, by connection id (`c1`).

Orientation.description:
`stream/put`'s `orientation`: how the picture is turned for display,
one of eight transforms by its lowercase name. Their numbers, 1 to 8,
follow the EXIF orientation tag's values, but 6 turns the picture a
quarter counterclockwise and 8 a quarter clockwise. A session
whose browser offered the video orientation extension carries it to
the browser, which turns the picture; others get it as the camera
sends it.

oneOf.description: 1: as the camera sends it.
2: mirrored left to right.
3: turned half way round.
4: flipped top to bottom.
5: turned a quarter counterclockwise, then flipped top to bottom.
6: turned a quarter counterclockwise.
7: turned a quarter clockwise, then flipped top to bottom.
8: turned a quarter clockwise.

Pong.description: The answer to `ping`, sent instead of a `result`.

SandboxInfo.description:
The hardening layers of the supervisor, so a client can warn the user
when one is missing.

ice.description: The ICE state, as the browser names it.

No control connection owns it; it closes when the grace expires
unless a `session/adopt` takes it back.

since.description: When the offer arrived, RFC 3339 UTC.

details.description: Protocol-specific detail, documented by the scheme's options schema.

url.description:
The URL redacted to its origin, `scheme://[****@]host[:port]`, then
`/****` when the path is anything but empty or `/` and `?****` when
a query is present: the path and query can carry secrets (a camera
key, a session token) as the userinfo can.

options.description:
Per-scheme options, typed by the scheme's factory; unknown fields
there are rejected too.

url.description:
The source URL, credentials included; redacted everywhere it is
reported.

Stream.description: A stream, as `stream/get` returns it and `stream/list` lists it.

last_error.description: The last error, if the stream is not live.

preload.description: Whether the stream stays connected without viewers.

since.description: When the current state began, RFC 3339.

StreamEvent.description:
An event of `stream/subscribe`.
Each variant's schema title names the Python client's class for it.

oneOf.description: The stream's state, first as it is, then on every change.
oneOf.title: StreamEventStream

oneOf.description: The stream was deleted.
oneOf.title: StreamEventStreamRemoved

created.description: The stream did not exist before.

StreamState.description: The connection state a stream shows.

oneOf.description: No demand, no worker.
Connecting to the source.
Media flows.
The source dropped; reconnecting at once.
Waiting out the reconnect delay.
Demand went away; the linger timer runs.
The worker crashed; the crash-backoff timer runs.

av_sync_lost.description:
Times the skew watchdog withdrew the stream's audio for sync; at
most 1, since it stays withdrawn while the source runs.

datagrams_rejected.description:
Datagrams refused before they were read (RTSP over UDP): from an
address other than the camera's media ports, not RTP, or from
another synchronization source.

frames_over_browser_limit.description:
Video frames the live path carried in more RTP packets than some
libwebrtc receivers assemble (2047), depending on their version;
every session sends them whole, and those viewers may freeze until
a keyframe that fits.

ingest_late_skips.description: Frames skipped as late after an ingest stall.

packets_lost.description:
RTP packets from the camera that never arrived, by their sequence
numbers: loss on the network (RTSP over UDP) or packets the camera
dropped itself.

packets_out_of_order.description:
RTP packets from the camera dropped because they came again or
after a later one (RTSP over UDP): duplicates and reordering.

Proportional set size (`Pss` of `smaps_rollup`): the shared text
pages divided among the processes mapping them, so the figures of
all processes add up.

counters arrive.

audio_delay_ms.description:
The delay a derived track's transcoder adds, in milliseconds; absent
on native tracks.

derived_from.description: The native track a derived track came from.

sync.description:
How the track is timed now: `arrival` until the camera's first
Sender Report for it, `sender_reports` from then on, `arrival` again
on a new timeline until the next report; at most a second old. A
derived track's is its source's.
